# Section documentation for [STACK-Maxima](../../index.md) /linearalgebra/vectors

Row and column vector notation available in core STACK. Use `vec_convert` to obtain
ordinary Maxima matrices for arithmetic and answer tests. The existing `c` and `r`
notation remains available through `stack_linear_algebra_declare(true)`.


---


## column_vector([entries])<a id='column_vector'></a>

A column vector with comma-separated components, for example `column_vector(a,b,c)`.
It is available without calling `stack_linear_algebra_declare` and displays
using the question's matrix delimiters.

This is inert notation: it keeps its column-vector identity instead of immediately
evaluating to a matrix. Use `vec_convert` for matrix arithmetic and answer tests:
`vec_convert(column_vector(a,b,c))` gives `matrix([a],[b],[c])`.
Matrix and variable-size matrix inputs preserve this constructor in responses.

The legacy short form `c` is unchanged. Convert both expressions with
`vec_convert` when comparing different notation; the inert operators differ.
Empty notation retains its identity, but matrix conversion and input grids
inherit the existing limitations on empty matrices.



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| entries | expressions | the comma-separated vector components. |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| column_vector | the inert column-vector expression. |


---


## row_vector([entries])<a id='row_vector'></a>

A row vector with comma-separated components, for example `row_vector(a,b,c)`.
It is available without calling `stack_linear_algebra_declare` and displays
using the question's matrix delimiters.

This is inert notation: it keeps its row-vector identity instead of immediately
evaluating to a matrix. Use `vec_convert` for matrix arithmetic and answer tests:
`vec_convert(row_vector(a,b,c))` gives `matrix([a,b,c])`.
Matrix and variable-size matrix inputs preserve this constructor in responses.

The legacy short form `r` is unchanged. Convert both expressions with
`vec_convert` when comparing different notation; the inert operators differ.
Empty notation retains its identity, but matrix conversion and input grids
inherit the existing limitations on empty matrices.



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| entries | expressions | the comma-separated vector components. |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| row_vector | the inert row-vector expression. |
